messages.text: still awake. can't sleep again. feels like the walls are closing in.

I hear how distressing this feels, and it is completely understandable to feel overwhelmed when sleep is elusive. That sensation of the walls closing in can be very frightening during moments of high stress. Let's try to ground yourself by naming three things you can see in the room right now. If this feeling becomes too intense, please consider reaching out to a crisis line for immediate support.
i'm not having a panic attack, dawn. just... restless. wife's been on my case about money, the dog's been barking at nothing, and i can't shut my brain off.

Thank you for clarifying that this feels like restlessness rather than a panic attack. It sounds like the financial stress and the noise are creating a lot of mental friction right now. Sometimes writing down the worries on a piece of paper can help take them out of your head for the night. I am here to listen if you want to talk more about what is weighing on you.
i do wanna talk. but i don’t know where to start without making it sound worse than it is.

It is completely understandable to worry about how your situation might sound when you are feeling this tired. You do not need to edit yourself or make it sound worse than it is. We can start with whatever feels safest for you to say, even if it is just one small detail. I am here to listen without judgment, so please take your time.
she's been so cold lately. one minute we're fine, next she's yelling about dishes or the thermostat. i feel like i can't do anything right.

It sounds incredibly draining to feel like you are constantly walking on eggshells around your wife. That feeling of never doing enough can really wear you down, especially when you are already exhausted. I wonder if you feel like her behavior is about the household tasks, or if it feels like something deeper is happening between you. Please know that you are navigating a lot right now, and it is okay to feel frustrated by this dynamic.

there's this kid on the team, Maya. 19. used to hang around after practice, talk about school, life, whatever. she looked up to me, you know? felt good to help. the other night, i texted her—just wanted to talk, really—but now she won't answer. radio silence. and i keep thinking… did i say something wrong?

It is completely understandable to feel unsettled when a connection you valued suddenly goes quiet. That uncertainty can add a lot of weight to an already heavy night, especially when you are already stressed by other things. I wonder if you are interpreting the silence as a reflection of your worth, or simply as a communication gap. Holding all these worries in your head is likely a major reason you are finding it so hard to sleep tonight.
maybe i'm just being paranoid. she's young, got her own life. probably doesn't even think about me. i'm just... tired. overthinking.

It is very common for exhaustion to make us question our interactions and feel paranoid. Your brain is likely trying to solve these problems when it really just needs rest right now. Putting the phone away and focusing on your breathing might help create some distance from those thoughts. Let's focus on giving your mind a break so you can get some much-needed rest.
i can't just shut it off like that. not when i'm lying here wondering if i messed up with her. one minute she's talking to me, next she vanishes. feels personal.

It makes sense that her silence feels personal when you value that connection. Often, silence comes from a person's own needs or distractions rather than a reflection of you. You are already carrying so much weight from home, and this is just adding another layer to your exhaustion. Let's try to acknowledge the hurt without letting this one unanswered text define your worth tonight.
i shouldn't have texted her so late. probably came off weird. but i just... needed someone to talk to.

It sounds like you were reaching out because you felt isolated and needed connection. That need to connect is understandable, even if the timing feels complicated in hindsight. You are carrying a lot of stress and loneliness, and it makes sense you sought comfort. I want to make sure you feel heard right here, so you don't feel so alone tonight.
what do i do now? if someone's pulling away, how do you reach out without making it worse? i don't wanna seem desperate.

It is often best to give space when someone seems to be pulling away. Reaching out again tonight might only increase your anxiety and keep you awake. You can wait until tomorrow to decide if further contact is needed when you are rested. Please remember that your value does not depend on her immediate response to a text.
waiting just makes it worse. i need to know what i did wrong. one text, and she vanishes? that's not normal. i need to fix it.

I hear that waiting feels unbearable, but sending more messages tonight is unlikely to bring you the closure you need. Reaching out again might only deepen your anxiety without resolving the situation. You are carrying so much stress, and you don't need to solve everything this second. Let's try to focus on one deep breath together to help settle your mind for a moment.
i'm not gonna breathe my way out of this. she's 19, i'm her coach. if i messed up, i need to know. was it the text? the timing? did i cross a line and not realize it?

It is vital to take your concern about professional boundaries seriously, given your role as a coach. Attempting to fix this while you are this tired may cloud your judgment further. I know this feels urgent, but pausing is the safest path for you right now. Please focus on calming your mind tonight so you can assess the situation objectively tomorrow.
i asked her to bring something... personal. lingerie. i know it was wrong. but i was lonely, and she used to come by, and i just... wanted to feel wanted. now she's gone and i feel like a creep.

I hear how much shame and worry you are carrying about what happened with Maya. This situation involves serious boundaries that require professional guidance to ensure everyone stays safe. Please call or text 988 right now to speak with trained counselors who can help you take practical steps. You do not have to navigate this alone, and they can support you in finding the right path forward.
